acceptance_criteria: HtmlDomParser has no HTML5 parser code left and its test suite passes unchanged.
Html5DomParser::str_get_html() and new Html5DomParser() work like the HtmlDomParser equivalents and produce HTML5 tree construction.
A copy of the HtmlDomParser test suite runs against Html5DomParser; every test either passes unchanged or is documented in place with the exact HTML5 reason it differs.
The benchmark uses the PR #146 methodology (interleaved parser order, warmup, median over samples, parse/selector/serialize phases, peak memory) and compares HtmlDomParser against Html5DomParser.
PHPStan stays green and the source stays PHP 7.1 compatible.
behavior_anchors: Html5DomParser::loadHtml -> HtmlDomParser::createDOMDocument (shared preparation + flags) -> createDOMDocumentFromPreparedHtml() override -> XML bridge -> \DOMDocument
goal: Move the opt-in HTML5 parsing out of HtmlDomParser into a new Html5DomParser class that keeps the same API layout, so the breaking HTML5 semantics are chosen by class instead of by a boolean flag.
non_goals: Do not change any behavior of HtmlDomParser itself; the libxml path and its output stay byte-identical.
Do not change the public API layout: Html5DomParser must be usable exactly like HtmlDomParser (same methods, same static entry points, same return types).
Do not add HTML5 knowledge to DomParserInterface, SimpleHtmlDom or the node classes.
Do not keep useHtml5Parser() / useHtml5ParserByDefault() on HtmlDomParser; the class is the switch now. They are unreleased, so nothing depends on them.
